rubric: MITHQAL v24.2.1 TGRS (Tokenized Gold Reserve Score)

thresholds.eligible: TGRS >= 8.0 AND all 13 eligibility conditions PASS
thresholds.conditional: TGRS >= 6.0 AND all 13 eligibility conditions PASS
thresholds.rejected: TGRS < 6.0 OR any of 13 eligibility conditions FAIL or UNCERTAIN

confidence_note: Scores are grounded in publicly verifiable issuer documentation, regulatory filings, and independent attestation reports retrieved via web-search and web-reader. Items marked UNCERTAIN could not be definitively verified from public sources and are flagged honestly per the rubric's 'do not assume PASS' constraint.

products.issuer: Paxos Trust Company LLC (now OCC National Trust, Charter #25379)
products.backing_unit: 1 fine troy ounce of allocated LBMA-grade gold per PAXG

1_IdentifiablePhysicalGoldBacking.evidence: Each PAXG corresponds to identifiable allocated gold bars; bar serial numbers and fine troy ounces are published in monthly attestation reports.

2_LegallyEnforceableOwnership.evidence: PAXG terms grant holders ownership rights in allocated gold; Paxos operates as a NYDFS-limited purpose trust company (now OCC national trust) under NY Banking Law.

3_AllocatedCustody.evidence: Allocated (not pooled) gold in LBMA-approved vaults; per Paxos documentation.

4_Segregation.evidence: Allocated bars are segregated and identifiable; holder claims run to specific physical bars.

5_BankruptcyRemoteness.evidence: Assets held in Paxos Trust Company bankruptcy-remote trust structure separate from Paxos corporate assets, under NY Banking Law and OCC trust supervision.

6_NoRehypothecation.evidence: Allocated gold cannot be lent or rehypothecated per trust terms and NYDFS/OCC trust regulation.

7_IndependentReconciliation.evidence: Monthly attestation reports by independent auditors. WithumSmith+Brown PC (Withum) through Feb 2025; subsequent attestations under AICPA standards by continuing independent CPA firm.

8_IndependentValuation.evidence: LBMA benchmark pricing; attestation reports confirm fine troy ounces reconciled to token supply.

9_RedemptionRights.evidence: PAXG holders can redeem for physical allocated gold bars (subject to verification/fees) or USD via Paxos.

10_ApprovedOracleReferencePricing.evidence: LBMA gold price benchmark; Chainlink integration for on-chain price feeds.

11_LegalReview.evidence: NYDFS-approved under limited purpose trust charter (2019); subsequently approved by OCC for national trust conversion (Dec 2025).

12_TechnologyLedgerIntegrity.evidence: ERC-20 on Ethereum; CertiK formal verification scored 98%; smart contract source public on GitHub (paxosglobal/paxos-gold-contract).

13_OperationalContinuity.evidence: Operating since Sept 2019 without operational failure; regulated trust company with capital requirements; OCC trust conversion strengthens continuity.

PhysicalBacking.justification: 1:1 allocated LBMA-grade gold, monthly independent attestation, bar serial numbers published.

LegalTitle.justification: NYDFS/OCC-regulated trust charter; clear ownership rights in allocated gold. Minor uncertainty on retail redemption logistics.

Custody.justification: Allocated custody in LBMA-approved vaults; bankruptcy-remote trust. Minor concentration risk on custodian.

Redemption.justification: Physical delivery available but with KYC, fees, and operational friction for retail holders.

IssuerReliability.justification: Paxos is federally regulated trust (OCC Charter #25379). Slight ding: $48.5M NYDFS settlement (Aug 2025) for AML deficiencies (related to former BUSD partner, not PAXG).

OracleReliability.justification: LBMA gold benchmark plus Chainlink on-chain oracle integration; gold price oracle highly reliable.

Settlement.justification: ERC-20 on Ethereum; deep secondary-market liquidity; settled via major exchanges.

Liquidity.justification: Listed on Coinbase, Binance, Kraken, etc.; among the largest gold-backed tokens by market cap.

OperationalResilience.justification: Operating continuously since 2019; regulated trust with capital requirements and federal supervision.

Jurisdiction.justification: NYDFS trust charter and OCC national trust charter; strong US regulatory oversight.

products.backing_unit: 1 fine troy ounce of allocated physical gold per XAUT

1_IdentifiablePhysicalGoldBacking.evidence: Reserves report (gold.tether.to/reports) discloses 707,747+ fine troy ounces held by custodian; each XAUT backed >=1 fine troy ounce.

2_LegallyEnforceableOwnership.evidence: Per Tether Gold Terms of Sale and Service, holders have direct entitlement to underlying allocated fine troy ounces of gold.

3_AllocatedCustody.evidence: Allocated physical gold stored in Swiss vaults per Tether documentation.

4_Segregation.evidence: Allocated bars segregated per holder claim per Tether terms; BDO audits confirm.

5_BankruptcyRemoteness.evidence: TG Commodities Limited corporate structure and bankruptcy remoteness of gold holdings from Tether group affiliates not clearly disclosed in public documentation.

6_NoRehypothecation.evidence: Allocated gold under custody; rehypothecation prohibited per terms.

7_IndependentReconciliation.evidence: BDO Italia (Big Four network) provides independent audit/reserves reporting for XAUT.

8_IndependentValuation.evidence: LBMA benchmark price used for valuation; BDO attestation.

9_RedemptionRights.evidence: Per ToS, verified holders can redeem XAUT for physical delivery of underlying gold bars (minimum 430 XAUT) or USD fiat.

10_ApprovedOracleReferencePricing.evidence: LBMA gold price reference; widely used pricing feeds.

11_LegalReview.evidence: Tether group has prior regulatory settlements (NYAG 2021, CFTC 2021) concerning USDT transparency; XAUT-specific legal review not separately published or approved by a major regulator.

12_TechnologyLedgerIntegrity.evidence: ERC-20 on Ethereum and TRC-20 on Tron; smart contracts publicly auditable on-chain.

13_OperationalContinuity.evidence: Operating since Jan 2020; largest gold-backed stablecoin by market cap (>US$4B as of early 2026).

products.eligibility_gate: FAIL (11/13 PASS, 2 UNCERTAIN: bankruptcy remoteness, legal review)

LegalTitle.justification: Direct entitlement per ToS but Tether corporate opacity introduces legal uncertainty.

Custody.justification: Allocated Swiss vaults; specific custodian identity not always prominently disclosed.

Redemption.justification: Physical delivery available but 430 XAUT minimum (~US$2M+) excludes retail holders.

IssuerReliability.justification: Tether group's historical opacity, NYAG/CFTC settlements, and incomplete USDT audits reduce issuer confidence; XAUT is separately audited but issuer reputation weak.

OracleReliability.justification: LBMA benchmark reference; widely used pricing infrastructure.

Settlement.justification: ERC-20 + TRC-20 dual-chain; large liquidity and broad exchange support.

Liquidity.justification: Largest gold-backed stablecoin globally; deep market across major exchanges.

OperationalResilience.justification: Operational since 2020 with no major gold-side incident, but broader Tether group operational risk.

Jurisdiction.justification: TG Commodities Limited is offshore (British Virgin Islands); less robust regulatory oversight than NYDFS/OCC trust.

8_IndependentValuation.evidence: LBMA benchmark gold pricing; audited at 999.9 fineness.

3_AllocatedCustody.evidence: Custody arrangement discontinued with product sunset.

3_AllocatedCustody.evidence: Historically allocated custody in Singapore; current status unverified.

2_LegallyEnforceableOwnership.evidence: ToS Clause 5A: compulsory redemption will entail 'CGT tokens ceasing to be backed by gold and no longer being recognized, honored, or redeemable by CACHE'; legal title being extinguished.

3_AllocatedCustody.evidence: Custody arrangement being wound down per issuer announcement.

5_BankruptcyRemoteness.evidence: Cache Private Limited is being wound up; assets not bankruptcy-remote in practice.

6_NoRehypothecation.evidence: Allocated gold not rehypothecated historically; wind-down does not allege rehypothecation.

7_IndependentReconciliation.evidence: Token audit publicly verifiable; independent audit history exists.

9_RedemptionRights.evidence: Compulsory redemption being conducted; holders receive equivalent value of PAXG tokens (subject to eligibility).

11_LegalReview.evidence: No public regulatory approval; wind-down being conducted under private terms.

12_TechnologyLedgerIntegrity.evidence: ERC-20 on Ethereum; token audit passed historically.

13_OperationalContinuity.evidence: Issuer publicly announced closing down operations.

products.issuer: Aurus Ecosystem (decentralized — multiple independent refineries/brokers participate)
products.backing_unit: 1 gram of allocated gold per tXAU (varies by participating issuer)

1_IdentifiablePhysicalGoldBacking.evidence: Each tXAU backed by 1g allocated gold from participating refineries; Aurus protocol aggregates supply.

2_LegallyEnforceableOwnership.evidence: Legal title framework varies by participating refinery/broker; decentralized issuance means no single consistent legal regime.

3_AllocatedCustody.evidence: Allocated custody at each participating refinery; protocol-level aggregation.

4_Segregation.evidence: Varies by participant; protocol does not enforce uniform segregation standard.

5_BankruptcyRemoteness.evidence: Decentralized participant structure means bankruptcy remoteness depends on each individual participant; no central bankruptcy-remote vehicle.

6_NoRehypothecation.evidence: Protocol rules may prohibit but enforcement varies by participant.

7_IndependentReconciliation.evidence: No single central auditor; per-participant attestation creates inconsistency.

9_RedemptionRights.evidence: Redeemable per protocol; specific redemption pathway varies by participant.

11_LegalReview.evidence: No centralized legal review; multi-jurisdictional participant model.

12_TechnologyLedgerIntegrity.evidence: ERC-20 on Ethereum / Polygon; smart contracts publicly verifiable.

13_OperationalContinuity.evidence: Aurus protocol operating since 2020 with growing participant network.

PhysicalBacking.justification: Allocated gold per token but backing quality varies by participant refinery.

LegalTitle.justification: Decentralized issuance creates inconsistent legal frameworks.

Custody.justification: Varies by participant; no uniform custody standard.

Redemption.justification: Redeemable but pathway varies; less standardized.

IssuerReliability.justification: No central issuer; protocol reliability depends on participant network.

OperationalResilience.justification: Protocol-level resilience depends on Aurus team; participant network fragmentation.
